gap: No result ChatGPT got states that SwitchBot's $149.99 Video Doorbell already includes its indoor monitor, but that screen is 4.3 inches at 480 × 272. eufy's E340 + Smart Display E10 gives an 8-inch 1,280 × 800 screen for $419.99 on eufy US today, $270 more and $20 above the $399.98 on ChatGPT's card.
standout_why: Smart Home Perfected, the cited rival (updated 2026-10-30), gives no prices; it says only 'Check Price On Amazon'. It does not list the E10's display size and gives no monitor resolution for SwitchBot. The WorthRated list gives no dollar prices and names only wired intercoms (LUMOBELL, TMEZON, AMOCAM). Reolink's own guide names no Reolink indoor screen and lists no prices. None of these pages sets the two ChatGPT cards side by side on price and screen resolution.
decides: This confirms that the shopper's choice is between ChatGPT's two cards, and it gives the trade-off as numbers. SwitchBot is the value pick at $149.99 with the monitor in the box, but PCWorld lists 'very low display resolution' as a con. eufy is the pick for screen quality: 8 inches at 1,280 × 800, a live feed that comes up when someone rings, and 64 GB storage in the display. It now costs $419.99, not the $399.98 the shopper saw. A TMEZON wired Wi-Fi 7-inch kit at $179.99 is the budget route if a 2-wire run is acceptable. Our AOSU doorbells come with a chime/storage base, and their listings name no screen, so they don't answer this question.
